config.title: Test Async Component

intro.title: Test Async Component
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Vue component that fetches and displays data from a mock API, simulating real-world asynchronous operations. You will learn how to use Vue's Composition API with the ref and onMounted functions to manage reactive state and handle side effects. The core concept covered is asynchronous programming in Vue, including making HTTP requests and updating the UI based on the response. By the end, you will understand how to test and implement async components effectively in a Vue application.
intro.usecase: Testing async components is essential for building reliable user interfaces that fetch data dynamically. In real applications, you'll test components that load user profiles from APIs, display real-time dashboard metrics, or handle form submissions with server validation. For example, when a shopping cart component fetches updated pricing or an admin panel loads analytics data, thorough async testing ensures these critical features work correctly under various network conditions. Mastering these tests helps prevent bugs in production where users interact with loading states, error messages, and dynamic content updates.

objectives: Implement a Vue component that fetches and displays asynchronous data
Configure loading states and error handling for async operations
Initialize and manage reactive data properties for async component state
Bind async data to template elements using Vue directives
Construct mock API responses for testing async component behavior
Integrate lifecycle hooks to control when async data is fetched
Render conditional UI elements based on async data loading status

steps.title: Import Vue and defineAsyncComponent
steps.instruction: Import Vue and the defineAsyncComponent function from the 'vue' package.
steps.hint: Use a named import to bring in both Vue and defineAsyncComponent from the 'vue' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing from a package
import { ref, computed } from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: The Vue library and defineAsyncComponent function are available for use in your component.
successCriteria: Vue and defineAsyncComponent are imported from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both Vue and defineAsyncComponent from the 'vue' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import Vue and defineAsyncComponent from the 'vue' package to proceed.

steps.title: Create the async component function
steps.instruction: Create an async function named 'asyncComponent' that returns a Promise resolving to a simple component object with a template property.
steps.hint: Use the async keyword before function, and return a Promise that resolves to an object containing a template string.
steps.seedCode:

// Create an async function named 'asyncComponent' that returns a Promise resolving to a simple component object
steps.expectedOutcome: The asyncComponent function is defined and ready to be used with defineAsyncComponent.
successCriteria: An async function named 'asyncComponent' is created that returns a Promise resolving to a component object with a template property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the function is async and returns a Promise that resolves to an object with a template property.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the function name and structure. It should be an async function returning a Promise with a component object.

steps.title: Use defineAsyncComponent to create async component
steps.instruction: Call defineAsyncComponent with your asyncComponent function and assign it to a variable named 'AsyncComponent'.
steps.hint: Use the defineAsyncComponent function imported earlier, passing your asyncComponent function as its argument.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: wrapping an async function with defineAsyncComponent
const AsyncComponent = defineAsyncComponent(asyncComponent);
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a variable named AsyncComponent that holds the async component created by defineAsyncComponent.
successCriteria: The AsyncComponent variable is defined using defineAsyncComponent with asyncComponent as its argument.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling defineAsyncComponent with asyncComponent and assigning it to a variable named AsyncComponent.
steps.feedbackWrong: call defineAsyncComponent with your asyncComponent function and store the result in a variable named AsyncComponent.

steps.title: Create main Vue component
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named 'App' with a setup function that returns an empty object.
steps.hint: Define a new component using the Vue composition API's setup function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The main Vue component 'App' is defined with a setup function that returns an empty object.
successCriteria: A component named 'App' is created with a setup function that returns an empty object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined a component named 'App' with a setup function that returns an empty object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The main Vue component wasn't created correctly. Create a component named 'App' with a setup function that returns an empty object.

steps.title: Import async component in main component
steps.instruction: Inside your App component's setup function, import the AsyncComponent variable that was created with defineAsyncComponent.
steps.hint: You need to bring the AsyncComponent into the scope of your main component so you can use it in the template.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AsyncComponent variable is imported and made available within the App component's setup function.
successCriteria: AsyncComponent is imported inside the setup function and returned from the setup function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing AsyncComponent (not asyncComponent) and returning it from the setup function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The async component needs to be imported inside the setup function. Try adding 'const AsyncComponent = ...' inside setup() and returning it.

steps.title: Register async component locally
steps.instruction: In your main component 'App', add a 'components' property that registers 'AsyncComponent' locally.
steps.hint: The 'components' option is an object where keys are component names and values are the imported components.
steps.expectedOutcome: The async component is registered locally in the main component, making it available for use in the template.
successCriteria: The 'App' component has a 'components' property with 'AsyncComponent' registered.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added a 'components' property to 'App' and included 'AsyncComponent'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The async component is not registered locally. Check that you've added the 'components' option correctly.

steps.title: Add loading state variable
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function of your App component, use Vue's ref to create a reactive loading state variable named isLoading and initialize it to true.
steps.hint: Remember to import ref from 'vue' if you haven't already. Then declare const isLoading = ref(true); inside setup().
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component's setup function now contains a reactive isLoading state variable initialized to true.
successCriteria: The setup function includes a const isLoading = ref(true); declaration.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've declared isLoading using ref() and initialized it to true inside the setup function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The loading state variable isn't properly set up. Check that you're using Vue's ref function to create a reactive variable named isLoading with an initial value of true.

steps.title: Add template structure with conditional rendering
steps.instruction: In the App component's setup function, return a template object with a root div element that conditionally shows a loading message when loading is true using v-if.
steps.hint: Use the loading variable from the previous step in a v-if directive on an element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component now has a template that conditionally renders a loading message based on the loading state variable.
successCriteria: The setup function returns a template object with a root div element containing a v-if directive that references the loading variable.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your template has a v-if directive that checks the loading variable and shows a loading message.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template structure with conditional rendering isn't quite right. Check that you're using v-if with the loading variable in the returned template object.

steps.title: Render async component when loaded
steps.instruction: In the template's v-else block, add the async component tag to render the AsyncComponent when loading is false.
steps.hint: Use the component name as a custom HTML tag inside the v-else block.
steps.analogousExample: // Example: rendering a component conditionally
steps.expectedOutcome: The async component will be displayed in the UI once it finishes loading, replacing the loading message.
successCriteria: The AsyncComponent tag is placed inside the v-else block of the template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the async component tag is placed in the v-else block.
steps.feedbackWrong: The async component should be rendered in the v-else block when loading is false.

steps.title: Simulate async loading delay
steps.instruction: In the asyncComponent function, wrap the returned object in a setTimeout to simulate a 2-second loading delay before resolving.
steps.hint: Use setTimeout with a callback that returns the component object. The delay should be 2000 milliseconds.
steps.expectedOutcome: The async component will now take 2 seconds to load, showing the loading message during the delay.
successCriteria: The asyncComponent function uses setTimeout with 2000ms delay before returning the component object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the setTimeout wraps the return statement and has a 2000ms delay.
steps.feedbackWrong: The asyncComponent function should use setTimeout to delay the component resolution. Try wrapping the return statement in setTimeout(() => { ... }, 2000).
